title: Lesson 12 - Harmonizing and consolidating multi-source data, canonical modeling, hierarchy management
description: Compare and contrast approaches for harmonizing and consolidating data from multiple sources, including canonical modeling techniques and hierarchy management, so you can establish a consistent master representation across systems.

questions.question: Four source systems must feed two target systems. Which mapping approach minimizes effort and future change?
options: Point-to-point mapping between every source and target
A canonical model that each source maps into, and each target maps from
A single flat mapping spreadsheet per source
questions.explanation: A canonical hub-and-spoke model reduces N*M point-to-point mappings to N+M and isolates change; the others scale poorly or bypass harmonization.

questions.question: Which TWO tasks belong to harmonization (before consolidation)?
options: Reconciling different code sets and date/address formats across sources
Applying survivorship rules to pick the winning attribute
Standardizing units and value domains to a canonical set
Writing the golden record back to source systems
questions.explanation: Harmonization makes values comparable (A, C) before you merge; survivorship (B) is part of consolidation and write-back (D) is a publish/co-existence step.

questions.question: A company needs both a legal entity hierarchy and a management/reporting hierarchy that differ. How should this be modeled?
options: A separate hierarchy object (junction) supporting multiple hierarchy types
Two parent fields on the same record
A text field holding the hierarchy path
questions.explanation: A single parent field supports only one hierarchy, so multiple hierarchies need a hierarchy-object/junction model; text paths are unmanageable and two parent fields is not a native pattern.
